Dnipro Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Dnipropetrovs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Dnipro was home to a substantial Karaite community alongside its much larger rabbinic Jewish population; the oldest surviving Karaite monument here, marking the grave of the colony's founder, dates to 1843. From 1907 to 1939, Dnipro's chief rabbi was Levi Yitzchak Schneerson — father of Menachem Mendel Schneerson, who became the most influential Chabad-Lubavitch Rebbe in modern history and transformed the movement into a truly global Jewish organization. An underground Lubavitch yeshiva operated here in the late 1920s and 1930s under leaders including Menachem Mendel Futerfas, later revered across the Chabad world as a legendary spiritual mentor and gulag survivor. On October 13–14, 1941, between 13,000 and 15,000 Jews were executed here over two days — one of the largest single massacres recorded anywhere in this collection — and more than 27,000 Jews from Dnipro and the surrounding area were killed in total. This is the oldest of Dnipro's documented Jewish cemeteries, now entirely overbuilt with private houses and other buildings; Dnipro's Jewish community remains one of the largest in Ukraine today, home to the Golden Rose Synagogue and the Menorah Center, among the largest Jewish community complexes in the world.
